Definition: from G5414; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety):--lade, by heavy laden.
BiblicalUsage: Phortizo means to load up, to burden, and it appears where men are loaded down. Jesus tells the lawyers, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers, for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers, and He calls the heavy laden to come to Him for rest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the loaded man is the gospel's invitation: the lawyers load and never lift, and Jesus lifts what the lawyers load.
